title: Experiments and memory
purpose: When a test ends, a winner waits to ship, or someone asks whether we tried that before, open Experiments and memory to get a clear call on what worked, what to roll out and what we already know, so no test money is spent twice.
fires: The testing agency's slide of added-up lifts, the test tracker spreadsheet nobody updates, the chat thread where the result got lost, and the founder's memory as the only record.
not_for: A store with too few orders to read tests that also will not make bold changes, or anyone looking for a tool that runs the traffic split itself.

jobs.job: When a test passed its end date and nobody looked at it, tell me the result and the call to make today, so I stop paying for the losing version
jobs.circumstance: Tuesday morning, a checkout test ended 9 days ago, the agency has moved on to the next brief, half the shoppers still see the old version, and nobody owns the read

progress.functional: know the result and which version to keep, in one line
progress.emotional: stop carrying the nagging guilt of loose ends; feel the tests are under control
progress.social: show the team and the agency that tests end in decisions, not in silence

jobs.hire_today: the testing agency's end-of-test slide when it comes; often nothing, because reading a test needs an analyst the store does not have
jobs.fire: waiting for the agency to send the read; the test tracker spreadsheet with blank result cells

forces.push: the losing version still takes half the traffic every day
forces.pull: the result and a keep, drop or rerun call on the day the test ends
forces.habit: tests get read when someone remembers to ask
forces.anxiety: what if the read is wrong and I kill a version that was winning

jobs.little_hire: every morning a test reaches its read date

watch.metric: days from each test's planned read date to a recorded result, trailing 90 days

drives.metric: share of traffic sent to a known losing version, per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 5 of 8 ended tests had no result 2 weeks after their date. After: every read recorded within 2 days.
jobs.not_for: a store that runs 1 test a quarter and whose founder reads it the same day

jobs.job: When a test won weeks ago, make sure the winning version is live for every shopper and still live, so I bank the money I paid to find it
jobs.circumstance: the win was called in a meeting 6 weeks ago, the developer ticket sits in a backlog, and a theme update last week may have wiped it

progress.functional: know each winner is live on 100 percent of traffic and has not been undone
progress.emotional: stop the fear that the win was lost somewhere between the meeting and the site
progress.social: hold the developer or the agency to the rollout with a date

jobs.hire_today: the developer's ticket queue and the agency's word that it shipped
jobs.fire: trusting that 'we shipped it' means it is live; clicking around the site by hand to check

forces.push: a win on half the traffic earns half; theme and app updates quietly undo wins
forces.pull: every winner shown as live, partial or lost, with the dollars waiting
forces.habit: the win gets celebrated and then forgotten
forces.anxiety: what if the rollout breaks something the test never saw

jobs.little_hire: weekly, and after any theme, app or checkout update

watch.metric: share of called winners live on 100 percent of traffic within 14 days of the read
watch.source: brand brain (experiment registry) and a live check of the store

drives.metric: gross profit per visitor, store-wide, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 of 7 winners from last quarter are live for everyone. After: 7 of 7 within 14 days of the read.
jobs.not_for: a store whose tests are run and rolled out by one developer who ships the same day

jobs.job: When the team argues about whether a test 'worked', settle it with the rule we agreed before launch and the profit number, so the meeting ends in a decision
jobs.circumstance: Monday meeting, the agency says conversion is up 12 percent, the founder sees flat sales, the media buyer says it was the new ads

progress.functional: one answer from the metric, window and rule set before launch, with the side numbers next to it
progress.emotional: stop the circular fight that eats the hour and leaves everyone sore
progress.social: be the fair judge, not the loudest voice or the person who built the test

jobs.hire_today: the agency's slide, the testing tool's 'winner' badge, an analyst friend, or the founder's gut
jobs.fire: the argument by slide and the green badge as the final word

forces.push: the same fight costs an hour a week and nothing gets rolled out
forces.pull: the result read against the written rule, with profit per visitor for each version
forces.habit: the person who ran the test calls the result
forces.anxiety: what if the rule itself was set wrong and we are bound to a bad call

jobs.little_hire: every read, and any meeting where someone says 'it worked'

watch.metric: share of test reads decided against a rule written before launch, trailing 90 days

drives.metric: gross profit per visitor, kept version versus the other, over the test window

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 of 6 reads end in 'let's run it longer'. After: 6 of 6 end in keep, drop or rerun, with the reason written.
jobs.not_for: a solo founder with no agency and no team to disagree with

jobs.job: When someone proposes a test, tell me if we tried it before and what happened, so I do not pay for the same answer twice
jobs.circumstance: a new marketer or a new agency proposes a free shipping bar; the founder half remembers a test about 18 months ago but cannot find it

progress.functional: find the past test, its result and the conditions it ran in
progress.emotional: stop feeling that the business walks in circles
progress.social: answer the new hire with facts, not 'I think we tried that once'

jobs.hire_today: the founder's memory, old slide decks in a shared drive, or a message to the person who left
jobs.fire: the founder's memory as the only record; digging through old decks

forces.push: a repeat test burns 4 weeks of traffic on a known answer
forces.pull: every past try of the idea on this store, with result, date and what was different
forces.habit: it is easier to just test it again than to dig
forces.anxiety: what if the old test was badly run and the idea deserves a fresh shot

jobs.little_hire: every time a new test is proposed, and when a new person joins

watch.metric: tests launched that repeat a past idea with no new reason written, per quarter

drives.metric: share of test slots spent on new questions, per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 of 10 tests last year repeated an older one. After: 0 repeats without a written reason.
jobs.not_for: a new store with no test history yet

jobs.job: When a site change went live without a test, like a new theme, tell me honestly whether it helped or hurt, so I can undo a bad change fast
jobs.circumstance: 3 weeks after a new theme launched, sales are down 8 percent; the agency that built it says it is the season, the founder is not sure

progress.functional: separate the change from the season, the ads and the traffic mix, and say how sure the answer is
progress.emotional: stop lying awake wondering if the new site is losing sales
progress.social: go back to the agency with evidence, not a feeling

jobs.hire_today: gut feel, the build agency's reassurance, or a friend who looks at GA4
jobs.fire: the build agency marking its own homework; waiting another month to see

forces.push: sales are down and every week of waiting may be lost money
forces.pull: an honest read with the other causes named and a clear roll back or keep call
forces.habit: a new site gets time to settle, so nobody questions it
forces.anxiety: what if I roll back a good theme because of a slow month

jobs.little_hire: 2, 4 and 8 weeks after any big site change

watch.metric: conversion rate and revenue per visitor, same traffic sources, 4 weeks before versus 4 weeks after, with season and ad spend noted

drives.metric: gross profit per visitor, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 weeks of debate and no decision. After: a call in 1 week; the mobile product page is rolled back and conversion recovers 0.4 points.
jobs.not_for: a store whose traffic mix changed so much at the same time that no fair read is possible; it needs a split test next time

jobs.job: When a test is about to go live, make us write down what winning and losing look like, the day we read it and when we stop, so nobody can spin the result later
jobs.circumstance: the day before launch, the agency wants to ship, and nobody has written the metric, the read date or the stop rule

progress.functional: one main metric, a read date, a stop rule and a scale rule on record before launch
progress.emotional: calm that the result will be judged fairly
progress.social: hold the agency or the team to terms set in advance

jobs.hire_today: a line in the agency's brief that is often skipped; often nothing, because it feels like paperwork
jobs.fire: launching on a verbal 'go'

forces.push: past results were spun after the fact to keep a retainer or a pet idea alive
forces.pull: a one-minute sheet before launch that makes the read automatic
forces.habit: we decide how to judge a test when the numbers come in
forces.anxiety: what if writing rules down slows every launch

watch.metric: share of tests launched with metric, read date, stop rule and scale rule on file

drives.metric: share of reads decided on the first look, without a rerun

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 of 9 running tests have a read date. After: 9 of 9 have all 4 before launch.
jobs.not_for: a store shipping clear repairs that need no test at all

jobs.job: When a test version wins on conversion but gave a bigger discount or brought smaller orders, tell me if it made more profit per visitor, so I do not roll out a winner that loses money
jobs.circumstance: the 15 percent off version converts 18 percent better, the agency calls it a win, the founder wonders what it did to margin

progress.functional: gross profit per visitor for each version, after product cost, discount and shipping
progress.emotional: not be fooled by a green number
progress.social: push back on the agency with the right number

jobs.hire_today: the agency reports conversion; a bookkeeper might redo it by hand; mostly nothing, because product cost is not in the testing tool
jobs.fire: the testing tool's conversion-only verdict

forces.push: past 'wins' quietly shrank margin
forces.pull: profit per visitor side by side for each version
forces.habit: conversion rate is the number everyone knows
forces.anxiety: what if the product cost data is out of date

jobs.little_hire: every read that touches price, offer, bundle or discount

watch.metric: gross profit per visitor for each version, over the test window
watch.source: store orders with product cost, brand brain (experiment registry)

drives.metric: gross margin, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the discount version wins on conversion but earns $0.40 less profit per visitor. After: the call goes to the full price version.
jobs.not_for: a store with no product cost on file; it must add costs first or the number is unavailable

jobs.job: When the test queue has 20 ideas and room for 2, pick the ones aimed at the biggest money leak, so our few test slots go where the profit is
jobs.circumstance: start of the month, traffic is enough for 2 tests, the agency, the founder and the designer each push a favourite

progress.functional: a short list ranked by the money at stake and the odds, tied to where shoppers drop off
progress.emotional: stop the worry that we test small things while a big leak runs
progress.social: settle whose idea goes first without politics

jobs.hire_today: the testing agency's backlog score, the founder's favourite, or whoever pushes hardest
jobs.fire: the loudest voice and the agency's self-scored backlog

forces.push: test slots are few and each one used on a small idea costs a month
forces.pull: each idea shown with the leak it targets and the dollars at stake

forces.anxiety: what if the ranking ignores what I know about my customers

jobs.little_hire: at the start of each month and when a slot opens

watch.metric: share of tests launched from the top 5 of the ranked list, per quarter

drives.metric: gross profit banked from rolled-out winners, per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 of 6 tests last quarter targeted checkout, where most shoppers drop. After: 4 of 6.
jobs.not_for: a store with one obvious broken step; fix it, do not rank it

jobs.job: When a test version is losing money, stop it on the rule we set, not on one bad day and not a month late, so I lose as little as possible
jobs.circumstance: day 6 of a 14 day price test, orders on the new price are down 15 percent, the founder wants to pull it, the agency says wait

progress.functional: know whether the loss has crossed the stop rule or is still normal noise
progress.emotional: not panic and not freeze
progress.social: back the call to the agency with the rule we both signed

jobs.hire_today: the media buyer's or testing agency's judgement; the founder's gut after a bad day
jobs.fire: daily peeking at the dashboard and the panic call

forces.push: each day a losing version runs costs orders
forces.pull: a clear 'stop now' or 'hold, day 6 of 14 is normal' with the dollars lost so far
forces.habit: check the numbers every morning and react
forces.anxiety: what if I kill it the day before it turns

jobs.little_hire: daily while any test with money at risk is live

watch.metric: days a losing version ran past its stop rule, per month

drives.metric: gross profit lost to losing versions, per month

jobs.not_for: a store whose tests carry no real money risk, such as copy on a low traffic page

jobs.job: When a test is proposed for a broken button or a missing size chart, tell me to just fix it, so we stop losing sales for 4 weeks to prove the obvious
jobs.circumstance: the agency puts a 'size chart on product page' test in the plan; shoppers have been asking for it in tickets for months

progress.functional: sort proposals into fix now and test, with the reason

jobs.hire_today: the agency's habit of testing everything, which bills more hours; or the founder's call
jobs.fire: testing as the default for every change

forces.push: a known defect costs sales every day it waits
forces.pull: a clear fix-now list with each item's cost of waiting
forces.habit: 'we test everything' feels rigorous
forces.anxiety: what if the 'obvious' fix hurts in a way we did not expect

jobs.little_hire: each time a test is proposed, and after each site audit

watch.metric: days from finding a clear defect to fixing it, per defect
watch.source: brand brain (experiment registry) and help desk tags

drives.metric: conversion rate on the fixed step, 14 days before versus after

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a missing size chart waited 5 weeks in the test queue. After: fixed in 2 days, test slot saved.
jobs.not_for: a change where both versions could honestly win; that one needs a test

jobs.job: When a month of tests ends flat, show me the win rate a healthy program gets, so I do not cut testing just before it pays off
jobs.circumstance: a co-founder says 'testing does not work, 5 tests and 0 wins'; the agency renewal is next week

progress.functional: see our win rate against the normal range and what the flat tests taught
progress.emotional: stop the sinking feeling that testing is money down a hole
progress.social: defend or cut the program to a co-founder with facts

jobs.hire_today: the agency's reassurance, or nothing
jobs.fire: judging the program on the last month's mood

forces.push: a flat month is about to kill the program
forces.pull: our win rate next to the 10 to 20 percent range for store tests, and the lessons banked
forces.habit: every test is expected to win
forces.anxiety: what if the range is an excuse for a bad agency

watch.metric: win rate of closed tests, trailing 90 days, against the expected range

drives.metric: gross profit banked from rolled-out winners, trailing 6 months

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 0 of 5 won this month, the program is about to be cut. After: 3 of 20 won in 6 months, inside the range, and they pay 4x the fees.
jobs.not_for: a store whose tests are badly sized or badly chosen; the win rate there is a symptom, not bad luck

jobs.job: When I am deciding whether to keep paying for testing, show me what the whole program earned against a small group left on the old site, so I renew or cut on proof
jobs.circumstance: the testing agency renewal is due, the fee is $8,000 a month, and its slide adds up 40 percent of lift from 9 tests

progress.functional: one honest number: profit per visitor for everyone versus a held-back group, per dollar of fees
progress.emotional: stop suspecting I am paying for a story
progress.social: renew or fire the agency with a number both sides accept

jobs.hire_today: the agency's own summed-lift slide
jobs.fire: the summed-lift slide as proof

forces.push: the fee is large and the store's sales do not show the claimed lift
forces.pull: a held-back group that shows the real gain
forces.habit: trusting the agency's math because it is the expert
forces.anxiety: what if the held-back group costs sales

jobs.little_hire: each quarter, and 30 days before any renewal

watch.metric: gross profit per visitor, all shoppers versus a 5 percent held-back group, 90 days
watch.source: store orders and brand brain (experiment registry)

drives.metric: gross profit banked per dollar of testing fees, per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the agency claims plus 40 percent. After: the held-back group shows plus 6 percent profit per visitor, worth 2.1x the fees.
jobs.not_for: a store with too little traffic to hold back a group and still read it

jobs.job: When I weigh a new idea, show me what happened every time this store tried something like it, so I start from our own record, not a blog post
jobs.circumstance: the agency cites a case study with a 30 percent lift; the founder remembers bundles never worked here

progress.functional: the brand's own results for this kind of idea, next to the general claim
progress.emotional: feel the business is learning, not starting over each time

jobs.hire_today: founder memory and the agency's general playbook
jobs.fire: the case study as the default belief

forces.push: outside claims keep leading to tests that flop here
forces.pull: our own track record per idea type, updated after each read
forces.habit: we trust famous brands' results more than our own
forces.anxiety: what if our old results came from bad tests

jobs.little_hire: each time a new idea is weighed

watch.metric: share of new test proposals that show this store's own past result for the idea type

drives.metric: win rate of new tests, trailing 6 months

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 0 proposals show our own history. After: every proposal shows it, and bundle tests stop after 3 flat tries.
jobs.not_for: a store with fewer than 5 closed tests; there is no record yet to read

jobs.job: When the week is full, tell me the one test decision that needs me and handle the rest, so testing does not stall on my calendar
jobs.circumstance: Thursday, 4 reads due, 2 launches waiting for a yes, and the founder is at a trade show

progress.functional: a short list of the calls only the founder can make, the rest taken care of
progress.emotional: stop feeling like the bottleneck
progress.social: let the team move without waiting on me

jobs.hire_today: a head of growth or an agency lead, or nothing, and tests wait
jobs.fire: tests waiting a week for the founder's reply

forces.pull: one decision a week that needs me, with a clear yes or no
forces.habit: the founder signs off on everything
forces.anxiety: what if something goes out I would have stopped

watch.metric: days tests wait for a founder decision, trailing 30 days

drives.metric: tests completed per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: tests wait an average of 6 days for a yes. After: 1 day; the founder makes 2 calls a week.
jobs.not_for: a founder who wants to approve every change personally

jobs.job: When a discount popup or a win-back email claims it made sales, measure it against a group that never saw it, so I stop paying discounts to people who would have bought anyway
jobs.circumstance: the email tool says the welcome discount made $40,000 last quarter; the founder suspects most buyers would have bought anyway

progress.functional: the extra orders and profit the discount actually caused
progress.emotional: stop the doubt every time the discount line shows in the books
progress.social: show the retention agency the real number

jobs.hire_today: the email tool's own attributed revenue; nothing, because holding back a group feels like losing sales

forces.anxiety: what if the held-back group loses real sales

jobs.little_hire: each quarter, and before changing any discount

watch.metric: orders and gross profit per person, shown the offer versus a held-back group, 30 days
watch.source: store orders, email tool and brand brain (experiment registry)

drives.metric: discount rate, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the tool credits the popup with $40,000. After: the held-back group shows $9,000 of real gain; the discount drops from 15 to 10 percent.
jobs.not_for: a store under about 2,000 subscribers a month, too small to hold back a group

jobs.job: When a test shows a huge win, check it for a setup error before we celebrate or bank it, so we do not plan the quarter around a fluke
jobs.circumstance: a new product page layout shows plus 45 percent; the agency is drafting a case study

progress.functional: check the split, the tracking and the dates before calling it
progress.emotional: avoid the crash after a fake win

jobs.hire_today: nothing; big wins get celebrated, not checked
jobs.fire: the celebration before the check

drives.metric: share of banked wins still ahead at 90 days

jobs.job: When a test is called a win, check 30 days later that returns, refunds and angry tickets did not rise, so a win on day 14 is not a loss on day 45
jobs.circumstance: a bold claim headline won; the support lead mentions more 'not as described' tickets

jobs.hire_today: nothing; the test tool stops counting at checkout and returns arrive weeks later in another system

watch.metric: return rate and refund rate of each version's buyers, 30 days after the read
watch.source: store orders, returns and help desk

jobs.job: When a test ends and some of the numbers are missing or broken, tell me it cannot be read and why, so I do not act on a false result

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 wrong calls last year from broken tracking. After: 0; both would have been flagged.
